\section{Filter Stability for Active SLAM}\label{sec:filter_stability}
    The Wasserstein filter stability error
    \eqref{eq:wasserstein_filter_stability} measures the merging of the two
    posteriors initialized at $b_t^-$ and $b^*$. We cannot invoke the
    contraction-based results of \citet{demirci2024refined} directly, as they
    require the state transition kernel to be mixing, which the SLAM
    kernel $\mathcal{S}=\mathcal{T}\otimes\delta_m$ violates through the static
    map. The product structure nonetheless permits separating the error into a
    pose contribution and a map contribution, which obey different mechanisms.
    The pose transition mixes, so its contribution decays geometrically in
    $N$ by the Hilbert-metric arguments of
    \cite{demirci2024refined,demirci2025unique}. The map is static, so its
    contribution is governed not by mixing but by posterior consistency.
    We treat the two in turn and assemble them into an asymptotic
    near-optimality result.
 
    \subsection{Decomposition of the Wasserstein Filter Stability Error}
    \label{sub:W1_decomposition}

    Fix a realization of the history of measurements $h_t^N\coloneq(y_{[t,t+N]},u_{[t,t+N-1]})$.
    The joint posterior on $\mathbb{S}$ initialized at prior $b$
    decomposes as
    \begin{equation*}
        \mathbb{P}^{b}(S_{t+N}\in(dx,dm)\mid h_t^N)
        =\mathbb{P}^{b}(X_{t+N}\in dx\mid M_{t+N}=m,\,h_t^N)\,
        \mathbb{P}^{b}(M_{t+N}\in dm\mid h_t^N),
    \end{equation*}
    and similarly for the posterior initialized at $b^*$.

    Introduce the intermediate measure
    \begin{equation*}
        \lambda(dx,dm)
        \coloneq\mathbb{P}^{b^*}(X_{t+N}\in dx\mid M_{t+N}=m,\,h_t^N)\,
        \mathbb{P}^{b_t^-}(M_{t+N}\in dm\mid h_t^N),
    \end{equation*}
    which pairs the pose conditional of $\mathbb{P}^{b^*}$ with the map
    marginal of $\mathbb{P}^{b_t^-}$. The triangle inequality for $W_1$
    on $(\mathbb{S},d_{\mathbb{S}})$ gives
    \begin{align}
        &W_1\!\bigl(\mathbb{P}^{b^*}\!\!(S_{t+N}\in\cdot\mid h_t^N),\;
        \mathbb{P}^{b_t^-}(S_{t+N}\in\cdot\mid h_t^N)\bigr)\nonumber\\
        &\le\underbrace{W_1\!\bigl(\mathbb{P}^{b^*}\!\!(S_{t+N}\in\cdot\mid h_t^N),\;
        \lambda\bigr)}_{\text{(M): map marginal}}
        +\underbrace{W_1\!\bigl(\lambda,\;
        \mathbb{P}^{b_t^-}(S_{t+N}\in\cdot\mid h_t^N)\bigr)}_{\text{(P):
        pose conditional}}.
        \label{eq:MP_decomposition}
    \end{align}
    % subsection Decomposition of the Wasserstein Filter Stability Error (end)

    \subsection{The Pose Term}\label{sec:Term (P): pose marginal} % (fold)
    We first aim to investigate the pose marginal:
    \begin{align}
        &W_{1}(\mathbb{P}^{b_{t}^{-}}(S_{t+N}\in \cdot \mid h_{t}^{N}),\lambda)
        \nonumber\\
        &=W_{1}(\mathbb{P}^{b_{t}^{-}}(X_{t+N}\in \cdot \mid M_{t+N}=m,h_{t}^{N})
        \mathbb{P}^{b_{t}^{-}}(M_{t+N}\in \cdot \mid h_{t}^{N}),\nonumber\\
        &\qquad\qquad\mathbb{P}^{b^{*}}(X_{t+N}\in \cdot \mid M_{t+N}=m,h_{t}^{N})
        \mathbb{P}^{b_{t}^{-}}(M_{t+N}\in \cdot \mid h_{t}^{N}))\nonumber\\
        &=\sup_{f:\lVert f \rVert _{Lip}\le 1}\left\{ \int\limits_{\mathbb{M}}
            \int\limits_{\mathbb{X}} f(x,m)\mathbb{P}^{b_{t}^{-}}(dx\mid
            M_{t+N}=m,h_{t}^{N})\mathbb{P}^{b_{t}^{-}}(M_{t+N}\in dm\mid
            h_{t}^{N})\right.\nonumber\\
            &\left.\qquad\qquad\qquad-\int\limits_{\mathbb{M}} 
            \int\limits_{\mathbb{X}} f(x,m)\mathbb{P}^{b^{*}}(dx\mid
            M_{t+N}=m,h_{t}^{N})\mathbb{P}^{b_{t}^{-}}(M_{t+N}\in dm\mid h_{t}^{N})
        \right\}\nonumber\\
        &=\sup_{f:\lVert f \rVert _{Lip}\le1} \left\{ 
            \int\limits_{\mathbb{M}} \int\limits_{\mathbb{X}} f(x,m)
            \left[ \mathbb{P}^{b_{t}^{-}}(dx\mid
            M_{t+N}=m,h_{t}^{N})-\mathbb{P}^{b^{*}}(dx\mid M_{t+N}=m,h_{t}^{N})
            \right]
            \mathbb{P}^{b_{t}^{-}}(dm\mid h_{t}^{N})\right\}\nonumber\\
        &\le \int\limits_{\mathbb{M}}\sup_{f:\lVert f \rVert _{Lip}\le1} \left\{
            \int\limits_{\mathbb{X}} f(x,m)
            \left[ \mathbb{P}^{b_{t}^{-}}(dx\mid
            M_{t+N}=m,h_{t}^{N})-\mathbb{P}^{b^{*}}(dx\mid M_{t+N}=m,h_{t}^{N})
            \right]\right\}
            \mathbb{P}^{b_{t}^{-}}(dm\mid h_{t}^{N})\nonumber\\
        &= \int\limits_{\mathbb{M}}W_{1}(\mathbb{P}^{b_{t}^{-}}(X_{t+N}\in
        \cdot \mid M_{t+N}=m,h_{t}^{N}),\mathbb{P}^{b^{*}}(X_{t+N}\in \cdot
        \mid M_{t+N}=m,h_{t}^{N})) \mathbb{P}^{b_{t}^{-}}(dm\mid
        h_{t}^{N})\nonumber\\
        &\le \int\limits_{\mathbb{M}}\frac{\mathrm{diam}(\mathbb{X})}{2}\lVert
        \mathbb{P}^{b_{t}^{-}}(X_{t+N}\in \cdot \mid
        M_{t+N}=m,h_{t}^{N})-\mathbb{P}^{b^{*}}(X_{t+N}\in \cdot \mid
        M_{t+N}=m,h_{t}^{N}) \rVert_{TV}  \mathbb{P}^{b_{t}^{-}}(dm\mid
        h_{t}^{N})\nonumber\\
        &\le \frac{\mathrm{diam}(\mathbb{X})}{\log 3}\int\limits_{\mathbb{M}}
        h(\mathbb{P}^{b_{t}^{-}}(X_{t+N}\in \cdot \mid
        M_{t+N}=m,h_{t}^{N}),\mathbb{P}^{b^{*}}(X_{t+N}\in \cdot \mid
        M_{t+N}=m,h_{t}^{N})) \mathbb{P}^{b_{t}^{-}}(dm\mid
        h_{t}^{N})\label{eq:hilbert_bound}
    \end{align}
    The second to last inequality uses the fact that
    $W_1(\mu,\nu)\le\mathrm{diam}(\mathbb{X})\lVert \mu-\nu\rVert_{TV}$ on the
    compact space $\mathbb{X}$, and the final line invokes the bound of
    the total variation distance by the Hilbert metric
    (Lemma~\ref{lem:hilbert_tv} below). It remains to control the Hilbert
    distance between the two conditional pose filters
    \begin{equation}
        \pi_m^{b}\coloneq\mathbb{P}^{b}(X_{t+N}\in\cdot\mid M_{t+N}=m,h_t^N),
        \qquad b\in\{b_t^{-},b^{*}\},
        \label{eq:condition_pose_filters}
    \end{equation}
    uniformly in $m$, and to exhibit geometric decay in the window size $N$.

    The key idea is that conditioning on $M_{t+N}=m$ reduces
    the recursion to the standard filter setup seen in past work such as in
    \citet{demirci2025unique}.  The two priors enter only through the initial
    conditional pose laws afterward both filters process the identical realized
    window of information. Thus both pose filters defined in
    \eqref{eq:condition_pose_filters} are two instances of the same filter
    driven by the same data from two different initializations, the standard
    setting for filter stability.

    We first define some technical properties
    \begin{definition}[Comparable]
        Two non-negative measures $\mu ,\mu '$ on
        $(\mathbb{X},\mathcal{B}(\mathbb{X}))$ are \textit{comparable}, if there
        exist positive constants $0<a\le b$ such that for any Borel subset 
        $A\subset \mathbb{X}$ 
        \begin{equation*}
            a\mu'(A)\le\mu (A)\le b\mu'(A).
        \end{equation*}
    \end{definition}
    \begin{definition}[Mixing kernel]
        The non-negative kernel $K$ defined on $\mathbb{X}$ is \textit{mixing},
        if there exists a constant $0<\epsilon \le 1$, and a non-negative 
        measure $\lambda $ on $\mathbb{X}$, such that $\forall x\in \mathbb{X}$ 
        and any Borel subset $A\subset \mathbb{X}$
        \begin{equation*}
            \epsilon \lambda (A)\le K(x,A)\le \frac{1}{\epsilon }\lambda (A).
        \end{equation*}
    \end{definition}
    Remark that a kernel $K$ is mixing only if $\forall x\in \mathbb{X}$
    there exists some reference measure $\lambda $ on $\mathbb{X}$ such that
    $K(x,\cdot ),\lambda $ are comparable.

    \begin{assumption}
        \label{ass:hilbert_mixing}
        \begin{enumerate}
            \item[]
            \item There exist constants $0<a_-\le a_+<\infty$ such that the pose
                transition kernel admits a density with respect to a reference
                measure $\lambda$ on $\mathbb{X}$ satisfying
                \begin{equation*}
                    a_-{\lambda(A)}\le{\mathcal{T}(A\mid x,u)}
                    \le a_+{\lambda(A)}
                    \qquad\forall x\in\mathbb{X},\ u\in\mathbb{U},\,\text{Borel }A\subset \mathbb{X}.
                \end{equation*}
            \item The observation density is bounded and everywhere positive:
            \begin{equation*}
                0<\underline{o}\coloneqq
                \inf_{(x,m,y)\in\mathbb{X}\times\mathbb{M}\times\mathbb{Y}}
                o(y\mid x,m)
                \le\sup_{(x,m,y)\in\mathbb{X}\times\mathbb{M}\times\mathbb{Y}}
                o(y\mid x,m)\eqqcolon\overline{o}<\infty.
            \end{equation*}
        \end{enumerate}
    \end{assumption}

    \begin{remark}
        Assumption~\ref{ass:hilbert_mixing}-(1) is satisfied on a compact
        $\mathbb{X}$ by any process noise with a continuous density
        that is bounded away from zero, such as Gaussian noise restricted to
        $\mathbb{X}$.
    \end{remark}
    We define the Hilbert metric.
    \begin{definition}[Hilbert metric]
        Let $\mu,\nu$ be two non-negative finite measures. We define the Hilbert
        metric on such measures as 
        \begin{equation}
            h(\mu ,\nu )=
            \begin{cases}
            \log \left( \frac{\sup _{A\mid \nu (A)>0}\frac{\mu (A)}{\nu (A)}}
            {\inf _{A\mid \nu (A)>0}\frac{\mu (A)}{\nu (A)}} \right) & 
            \text{if }\mu ,\nu \text{ are comparable}\\
             0&\text{if }\mu =\nu =0\\
             \infty &\text{else}
            .\end{cases}
            \label{eq:hilbert_metric}
        \end{equation}
    \end{definition}
    We remark that the metric is invariant under scaling,
    $h(a\mu,b\nu)=h(\mu,\nu)$ for $a,b>0$.

    The discussion that follows builds on \citet{demirci2025unique}, particularly
    drawing on two crucial lemmas.
    \begin{lemma}[{\cite[Lemma~3.9]{demirci2025unique}}]
        \label{lem:hilbert_tv}
        For non-negative finite measures $\mu,\mu'$ with normalizations
        $\bar\mu,\bar\mu'$,
        \begin{equation*}
            \lVert\bar\mu-\bar\mu'\rVert_{TV}\le\frac{2}{\log 3}\,h(\mu,\mu').
        \end{equation*}
    \end{lemma}
    \begin{lemma}[Birkhoff contraction coefficient
        {\cite[Lemma~3.11]{demirci2025unique}}]
        \label{lem:birkhoff}
        The nonnegative linear operator on $\mathcal{M}_+(\mathbb{X})$ 
        (positive measures on $\mathbb{X}$) associated with a nonnegative kernel
        $K$ defined on $\mathbb{X}$, is a contraction in the Hilbert metric
        with coefficient
        \begin{equation*}
            \tau_B(K)\coloneq\sup_{0<h(\mu,\nu)<\infty}
            \frac{h(K\mu,K\nu)}{h(\mu,\nu)}=\tanh\!\Big(\tfrac14 H(K)\Big),
            \qquad H(K)\coloneq\sup_{\mu,\nu}h(K\mu,K\nu),
        \end{equation*}
        and $H(K)<\infty$ implies $\tau_B(K)<1$.
    \end{lemma}

    We now establish the per-step contraction of the conditional pose filter.
    Fix $m\in\mathbb{M}$, $u\in\mathbb{U}$, $y\in\mathbb{Y}$ and, following
    \cite[Lemma~3.12]{demirci2025unique}, fold the prediction and correction
    into a single nonnegative kernel $K$ on $\mathcal{M}_+(\mathbb{X})$,
    \begin{equation*}
        K\mu(dx')\coloneq o(y\mid x',m)\int_{\mathbb{X}}
        \mathcal{T}(dx'\mid x,u)\,\mu(dx).
    \end{equation*}
    The conditional pose filter is the normalization of $K$, i.e.,
    $\mathbb{P}^{b}(X_{t+1}\in\cdot\mid M=m,X_t\sim\mu,y,u)
    =\overline{K\mu}$, where the bar denotes normalization. By scale invariance
    of $h$, this normalization is immaterial for the Hilbert distance.

    \begin{lemma}[One-step contraction]
        \label{lem:one_step_hilbert}
        Under Assumption~\ref{ass:hilbert_mixing}, for every $m\in\mathbb{M}$,
        $u\in\mathbb{U}$, $y\in\mathbb{Y}$ and all
        $\mu,\nu\in\mathcal{M}_+(\mathbb{X})$,
        \begin{enumerate}
            \item $H(K)\le\Delta\coloneq 2\log\dfrac{a_+}{a_-}$;
            \item $h(K\mu,K\nu)\le\alpha\,h(\mu,\nu)$, with
                $\alpha\coloneq\dfrac{a_+-a_-}{a_++a_-}<1$.
        \end{enumerate}
    \end{lemma}
    \begin{proof}
        For any $A\in\mathcal{B}(\mathbb{X})$,
        \begin{equation*}
            K\mu(A)=\int_A o(y\mid x',m)\left(\int_{\mathbb{X}}
            \mathcal{T}(dx'\mid x,u)\,\mu(dx)\right).
        \end{equation*}
        Recall Assumption~\ref{ass:hilbert_mixing}-(1): for all $x$ and all $A\in\mathcal{B}(\mathbb{X})$,
        \begin{equation*}
            a_{-}\lambda(A)\le \mathcal{T}(A\mid x,u)\le a_{+}\lambda(A).
        \end{equation*}
        Integrating each side against $\mu$ (a positive operation, so the inequalities are preserved) gives
        \begin{equation*}
            a_-\mu(\mathbb{X})\,\lambda(A)
            \le (\mu\mathcal{T})(A)
            \le a_+\mu(\mathbb{X})\,\lambda(A),
            \qquad (\mu\mathcal{T})(A):=\int_{\mathbb{X}}\mathcal{T}(A\mid x,u)\,\mu(dx),
        \end{equation*}
        so weighting by $o(y\mid\cdot,m)\ge 0$ and integrating over $A$, with
        the fixed measure $\Omega(A):=\int_A o(y\mid x',m)\,\lambda(dx')$,
        \begin{equation*}
            a_-\mu(\mathbb{X})\,\Omega(A)\le K\mu(A)\le a_+\mu(\mathbb{X})\,\Omega(A)
        \end{equation*}
        and likewise for $\nu$
        \begin{equation*}
            a_-\nu(\mathbb{X})\,\Omega(A)\le K\nu(A)\le a_+\nu(\mathbb{X})\,
            \Omega(A).
        \end{equation*}
        The factor $\Omega(A)$ cancels in the ratio,
        leaving for every $A$ with $K\nu(A)>0$,
        \begin{equation*}
            \frac{a_-}{a_+}\frac{\mu(\mathbb{X})}{\nu(\mathbb{X})}
            \le\frac{K\mu(A)}{K\nu(A)}
            \le\frac{a_+}{a_-}\frac{\mu(\mathbb{X})}{\nu(\mathbb{X})}.
        \end{equation*}
        The ratio of the supremum to the infimum is therefore at most
        $(a_+/a_-)^2$,
        \begin{equation*}
        H(K)=\sup_{\mu,\nu}h(K\mu,K\nu)\le\log \left( \frac{\frac{a_{+}\mu
        (\mathbb{X})}{a_{-}\nu (\mathbb{X})}}{\frac{a_{-}\mu
        (\mathbb{X})}{a_{+}\nu (\mathbb{X})}}
        \right)=\log\left(\frac{a_+}{a_-}\right)^2= \Delta,
        \end{equation*}
        which yields (1).
        For (2), Lemma~\ref{lem:birkhoff} gives
        \begin{equation*}
            h(K\mu,K\nu)\le\tau_B(K)\,h(\mu,\nu),
            \qquad
            \tau_B(K)=\tanh\!\Big(\tfrac14 H(K)\Big)
            \le\tanh\!\Big(\tfrac12\log\frac{a_+}{a_-}\Big)
            =\frac{a_+-a_-}{a_++a_-}=\alpha,
        \end{equation*}
        using $\tanh(\tfrac12\log r)=(r-1)/(r+1)$ with $r=a_+/a_-$.
    \end{proof}

    \begin{proposition}[Geometric stability of the conditional pose filter]
        \label{prop:pose_hilbert_decay}
        Under Assumption~\ref{ass:hilbert_mixing}, for every $m\in\mathbb{M}$,
        every realization $(y,u)_{[t,t+N]}$ of the window, and every $N\ge 1$,
        \begin{equation*}
            h\bigl(\pi_m^{b_t^-},\pi_m^{b^*}\bigr)\le\Delta\,\alpha^{N-1},
        \end{equation*}
        with $\Delta$ and $\alpha$ as in Lemma~\ref{lem:one_step_hilbert}.
    \end{proposition}
    \begin{proof}
        For $k=0,\dots,N-1$, let $K_k$ denote the unnormalized one-step filter
        operator built from the control $u_{t+k}$ and the observation
        $y_{t+k+1}$: for any $\mu\in\mathcal{M}_+(\mathbb{X})$ and any
        $A\in\mathcal{B}(\mathbb{X})$,
        \begin{equation*}
            K_k\mu(A)=\int_A o(y_{t+k+1}\mid x',m)
            \left(\int_{\mathbb{X}}\mathcal{T}(dx'\mid x,u_{t+k})\,\mu(dx)\right).
        \end{equation*}
        Composing these operators over the window and normalizing produces the
        conditional pose law at time $t+N$: for each prior $b\in\{b_t^-,b^*\}$,
        \begin{equation*}
            \mathbb{P}^{b}\!\left(X_{t+N}\in\cdot \;\middle|\; M=m,\;
            Y_{[t+1,t+N]}=y_{[t+1,t+N]},\;
            U_{[t,t+N-1]}=u_{[t,t+N-1]}\right)
            =\overline{K_{N-1}\cdots K_0\,\mu_0^{b}},
        \end{equation*}
        where $\mu_0^{b}=\mathbb{P}^{b}(X_t\in\cdot\mid M=m)$ is the initial
        conditional pose law and the bar denotes normalization to a probability
        measure. Since normalization is multiplication by a positive scalar and
        $h$ is invariant under positive scaling of either argument, the quantity
        we must bound is
        \begin{equation*}
            h\!\left(K_{N-1}\cdots K_0\,\mu_0^{b_t^-},\;
            K_{N-1}\cdots K_0\,\mu_0^{b^*}\right).
        \end{equation*}
        Write $\rho_k^{b}\coloneq K_{k-1}\cdots K_0\,\mu_0^{b}$ for the unnormalized
        measure after $k$ steps, with $\rho_0^{b}=\mu_0^{b}$. Throughout,
        $a_-,a_+$ are the mixing constants defined in
        Assumption~\ref{ass:hilbert_mixing}-(1) and
        \begin{equation*}
            \Delta\coloneq\log\!\left(\frac{a_+}{a_-}\right)^{\!2},
            \qquad
            \alpha\coloneq\frac{a_+-a_-}{a_++a_-}
            =\tanh\!\left(\tfrac12\log\tfrac{a_+}{a_-}\right).
        \end{equation*}
        as seen in Lemma~\ref{lem:one_step_hilbert}.

        The initial
        laws $\mu_0^{b_t^-},\mu_0^{b^*}$ arise from different priors and need not
        be comparable, so $h(\rho_0^{b_t^-},\rho_0^{b^*})$ may be infinite. This
        does not obstruct the bound on $\rho_1$ as
        Lemma~\ref{lem:one_step_hilbert}-(1) bounds $h(K_0\mu,K_0\nu)\le\Delta$ as a
        supremum over \emph{all} pairs of nonnegative inputs $\mu,\nu$, with no
        comparability required of them. Applying it to $\mu_0^{b_t^-},\mu_0^{b^*}$,
        \begin{equation*}
            h(\rho_1^{b_t^-},\rho_1^{b^*})
            =h(K_0\mu_0^{b_t^-},K_0\mu_0^{b^*})\le\Delta.
        \end{equation*}
        Hence a single application of the kernel sends any two finite measures to
        within $\Delta$, and renders them comparable.

        For $k=1,\dots,N-1$ the
        measures $\rho_k^{b_t^-},\rho_k^{b^*}$ are images of a mixing kernel, hence
        comparable, so $h(\rho_k^{b_t^-},\rho_k^{b^*})<\infty$,
        Lemma~\ref{lem:one_step_hilbert}-(2) gives the contraction
        $h(K_k\mu,K_k\nu)\le\alpha\,h(\mu,\nu)$ on comparable inputs. Hence
        \begin{equation*}
            h(\rho_{k+1}^{b_t^-},\rho_{k+1}^{b^*})
            =h(K_k\rho_k^{b_t^-},K_k\rho_k^{b^*})
            \le\alpha\,h(\rho_k^{b_t^-},\rho_k^{b^*}).
        \end{equation*}
        Iterating from $h(\rho_1^{b_t^-},\rho_1^{b^*})\le\Delta$ across the $N-1$
        steps $k=1,\dots,N-1$,
        \begin{equation*}
            h(\rho_N^{b_t^-},\rho_N^{b^*})
            \le\alpha^{\,N-1}\,h(\rho_1^{b_t^-},\rho_1^{b^*})
            \le\Delta\,\alpha^{\,N-1}.
        \end{equation*}
        By the scale invariance noted above, $h(\rho_N^{b_t^-},\rho_N^{b^*})$
        equals the Hilbert distance between the two normalized conditional pose
        laws
        $\mathbb{P}^{b_t^-}(X_{t+N}\in\cdot\mid M=m,\,Y_{[t+1,t+N]}=y_{[t+1,t+N]},\,
        U_{[t,t+N-1]}=u_{[t,t+N-1]})$ and
        $\mathbb{P}^{b^*}(X_{t+N}\in\cdot\mid M=m,\,Y_{[t+1,t+N]}=y_{[t+1,t+N]},\,
        U_{[t,t+N-1]}=u_{[t,t+N-1]})$, which is the claim. The constants
        $\Delta,\alpha$ depend only on $a_-,a_+$, so the bound is independent of
        $m$ and of the realized window $(y,u)_{[t,t+N]}$.
    \end{proof}

    Substituting Proposition~\ref{prop:pose_hilbert_decay} into
    \eqref{eq:hilbert_bound} and using the fact that
    $\mathbb{P}^{b_t^-}(M_{t+N}\in\cdot\mid h_t^N)$ is a probability measure,
    \begin{align*}
        W_1\bigl(\mathbb{P}^{b_t^-}(S_{t+N}\in\cdot\mid h_t^N),\lambda\bigr)
        &\le\frac{\mathrm{diam}(\mathbb{X})}{\log 3}
        \int_{\mathbb{M}}h\bigl(\pi_m^{b_t^-},\pi_m^{b^*}\bigr)\,
        \mathbb{P}^{b_t^-}(dm\mid h_t^N)\\
        &\le\frac{\mathrm{diam}(\mathbb{X})\,\Delta}{\log 3}\,\alpha^{N-1}.
    \end{align*}
    This holds for every realization of $(Y,U)_{[t,t+N]}$, hence is deterministic
    and passes through the supremum over policies and the expectation unchanged.
    The pose contribution to the Wasserstein filter stability error therefore
    satisfies
    \begin{equation}
        \sup_{\hat\gamma\in\hat\Gamma}
        \mathbb{E}^{\hat\gamma}_{b_0^-}\bigl[\,\text{(P)}\,\bigr]
        \le K\,\alpha^{N},
        \qquad
        \alpha=\frac{a_+-a_-}{a_++a_-},
        \qquad
        K=\frac{4\,\mathrm{diam}(\mathbb{X})\,\log(a_+/a_-)}{\alpha\,\log 3},
        \label{eq:pose_term_bound}
    \end{equation}
    via $\alpha^{N-1}=\alpha^{-1}\alpha^{N}$. Since $\alpha<1$, the pose term
    decays geometrically in $N$ and vanishes as $N\to\infty$.

    \subsection{Term (M): map marginal}\label{sec:Term (M): map marginal}
    We now bound term~(M) of the decomposition
    \eqref{eq:MP_decomposition},
    \begin{equation}
        \text{(M)}
        =W_1\!\bigl(\mathbb{P}^{b^*}(S_{t+N}\in\cdot\mid h_t^N),\,
        \lambda\bigr)
        =\sup_{f:\lVert f \rVert _{\text{Lip}}\le 1}
        \left\{  \int f\,d\mathbb{P}^{b^*}(S_{t+N}\in\cdot\mid h_t^N) -\int
        f\,d\lambda\right\}
        \label{eq:term_M}
    .\end{equation}
    Recall from the definition of the intermediate measure $\lambda$ in
    \eqref{eq:MP_decomposition} that the two arguments of (M) share a common
    pose conditional and differ only in their map marginal.
    Our goal is to bound (M) by a $W_1$ distance between the two map
    marginals alone, on which posterior consistency results from the parameter
    estimation literature can be invoked.
 
        \subsubsection{Regularity of the test function} % (fold)
        \label{sub:map_regularity}
        To this end, fix $f\in\mathrm{Lip}(\mathbb{S},1)$ and define the
        test function
        \begin{equation*}
            g(m)\coloneq\int_{\mathbb{X}}f(x,m)\,
            \mathbb{P}^{b^*}(X_{t+N}\in dx\mid M_{t+N}=m,\,h_t^N).
        \end{equation*}
        Since the pose conditional is common to both arguments of (M),
        the expression of the RHS of \eqref{eq:term_M} can be rewritten as
        \begin{equation}
            \int f\,d\mathbb{P}^{b^*}(S_{t+N}\in\cdot\mid h_t^N)
            -\int f\,d\lambda
            =\int_{\mathbb{M}}g(m)\,
            \bigl[\mathbb{P}^{b^*}(M_{t+N}\in dm\mid h_t^N)
            -\mathbb{P}^{b_t^-}(M_{t+N}\in dm\mid h_t^N)\bigr]
            \label{eq:M_disintegration}.
        \end{equation}
        If $g$ is Lipschitz in $m$ with some constant $L_g$, the
        Kantorovich--Rubinstein representation of $W_1$ on $\mathbb{M}$
        bounds the right-hand side of \eqref{eq:M_disintegration} by
        $L_g\,W_1\bigl(\mathbb{P}^{b^*}(M_{t+N}\in\cdot\mid h_t^N),
        \mathbb{P}^{b_t^-}(M_{t+N}\in\cdot\mid h_t^N)\bigr)$, a distance
        between the map marginals as desired. Taking the supremum over
        $f\in\mathrm{Lip}(\mathbb{S},1)$ on the left of
        \eqref{eq:M_disintegration} then yields the same bound on (M). It
        thus suffices to find a Lipschitz constant $L_g$ for $g$, and the
        only thing we require of it is that it does not grow with the window
        length $N$.
     
        To this end we bound $|g(m)-g(m')|$ by the following two terms:
        \begin{align}
            &|g(m)-g(m')|
            \le\underbrace{\int_{\mathbb{X}}
            |f(x,m)-f(x,m')|\,
            \mathbb{P}^{b^*}(X_{t+N}\in dx\mid M_{t+N}=m,\,h_t^N)
            }_{\text{(M.i): Lipschitz of $f$ in $m$}}\nonumber\\
            &\quad+\underbrace{\biggl|
            \int_{\mathbb{X}}f(x,m')\,
            \bigl[\mathbb{P}^{b^*}(X_{t+N}\in dx\mid M_{t+N}=m,\,h_t^N)
            -\mathbb{P}^{b^*}(X_{t+N}\in dx\mid M_{t+N}=m',\,h_t^N)
            \bigr]
            \biggr|}_{\text{(M.ii): sensitivity of pose
            conditional to $m$}}.
            \label{eq:g_lipschitz_decomp}
        \end{align}

        Term (M.i) is controlled by the Lipschitz constant of $f$,
        since $f$ is $1$-Lipschitz on $\mathbb{S}$ and the pose conditional 
        is a probability measure,
        \begin{equation}
            \text{(M.i)}\le d_{\mathbb{M}}(m,m').
            \label{eq:Mi_bound}
        \end{equation}

        Term (M.ii) measures the sensitivity of the conditional pose law to
        the map argument, where the two
        filters share the prior $b^*$ but condition on different maps $m$
        and $m'$. The densities $o(\cdot\mid\cdot,m,u)$ and
        $o(\cdot\mid\cdot,m',u)$ differ at every one of the $N$ 
        steps, so a discrepancy of order $d_{\mathbb{M}}(m,m')$ is
        added at each step.

        Before proceeding we impose the following assumption:
        \begin{assumption}
            \label{ass:sensor_map_regularity}
            \begin{enumerate}
                \item[]
                \item The observation density is Lipschitz in the map,
                    i.e., there exists
                    $C_{\mathcal{O}}<\infty$ such that for all
                    $x\in\mathbb{X}$, $y\in\mathbb{Y}$, $u\in\mathbb{U}$,
                    and $m,m'\in\mathbb{M}$,
                    \begin{equation*}
                        \bigl|o(y\mid x,m,u)-o(y\mid x,m',u)\bigr|
                        \le C_{\mathcal{O}}\,d_{\mathbb{M}}(m,m').
                    \end{equation*}
                \item The reference prior is of product form,
                    $b^*=b^*_{\mathbb{X}}\otimes b^*_{\mathbb{M}}$ for some
                    $b^*_{\mathbb{X}}\in\mathcal{P}(\mathbb{X})$ and
                    $b^*_{\mathbb{M}}\in\mathcal{P}(\mathbb{M})$.
            \end{enumerate}
        \end{assumption}
        Now, with an eye toward bounding term (M.ii) we state the following
        intermediate result:
        \begin{proposition}
            \label{prop:pose_conditional_lipschitz}
            Let Assumptions~\ref{ass:hilbert_mixing}
            and~\ref{ass:sensor_map_regularity} hold. Then for every $N\ge1$, every
            realization $h_t^N=(y_{[t,t+N]},u_{[t,t+N-1]})$ of the window, and
            every $m,m'\in\mathbb{M}$,
            \begin{equation*}
                W_1\Bigl(\mathbb{P}^{b^*}\bigl(X_{t+N}\in\cdot\mid
                M_{t+N}=m,\,h_t^N\bigr),\;
                \mathbb{P}^{b^*}\bigl(X_{t+N}\in\cdot\mid
                M_{t+N}=m',\,h_t^N\bigr)\Bigr)
                \le L_{\mathbb{X}}\,d_{\mathbb{M}}(m,m'),
            \end{equation*}
            where
            \begin{equation*}
                L_{\mathbb{X}}
                \coloneq\frac{2\,\mathrm{diam}(\mathbb{X})\,
                C_{\mathcal{O}}}{\underline{o}\,(1-\alpha)\log 3},
                \qquad
                \alpha=\frac{a_+-a_-}{a_++a_-}.
            \end{equation*}
        \end{proposition}
        \begin{proof}
            Let $K_k^{m}$ be the one-step filter operator of
            Proposition~\ref{prop:pose_hilbert_decay} built from the map
            $m$, the control $u_{t+k}$, and the observation $y_{t+k+1}$, 
            \begin{equation*}
                K_k^{m}\mu(A)
                =\int_A o\bigl(y_{t+k+1}\mid x',m,u_{t+k}\bigr)
                \biggl(\int_{\mathbb{X}}\mathcal{T}(dx'\mid x,u_{t+k})\,
                \mu(dx)\biggr),
                \qquad A\in\mathcal{B}(\mathbb{X}),
            \end{equation*}
            and write
            \begin{equation*}
                \pi_k^{m}\coloneq K_{k-1}^{m}\cdots K_0^{m}\,\mu_0^{m}
            \end{equation*}
            which denotes the unnormalized conditional pose measure after applying
            $K_0^m,\dots,K_{k-1}^m$ to the initial law $\mu _{0}^{m}\coloneq
            \mathbb{P}^{b^*}(X_t\in\cdot\mid M=m)$. Write $\pi_k^{m'}$ for the
            pose measure initialized with map $m'$. 
           
            We aim to analyze the Hilbert distance
            $d_k\coloneq h(\pi_k^{m},\pi_k^{m'})$, which by scale invariance
            is unaffected by any normalization. 

            Because $b^*$ is a product
            measure, the two filters start from the same pose law
            $b^*_{\mathbb{X}}$, so 
            \begin{equation*}
                d_0=0.
            \end{equation*} 
            Fix $k$ and any
            $\mu\in\mathcal{M}_+(\mathbb{X})$. Let $\nu\in\mathcal{M}_+(\mathbb{X})$
            be the one-step predicted measure obtained by imposing action $u_{t+k}$
            on $\mu$,
            \begin{equation*}
                \nu(A)\coloneq\int_{\mathbb{X}}\mathcal{T}(A\mid x,u_{t+k})\,\mu(dx),
                \qquad A\in\mathcal{B}(\mathbb{X}),
            \end{equation*}
            which is common to both operators since $K_k^{m}$ and $K_k^{m'}$ share
            the pose kernel $\mathcal{T}$ and differ only in the map argument of the
            observation density. Let
            \begin{equation*}
                a(x')\coloneq o(y_{t+k+1}\mid x',m,u_{t+k}),
                \qquad
                b(x')\coloneq o(y_{t+k+1}\mid x',m',u_{t+k}).
            \end{equation*}
            Now the definition of the one-step filter operator can be
            re-interpreted as the reweighting of $\nu$ by the corresponding
            density:
            \begin{equation*}
                K_k^{m}\mu(dx')=a(x')\,\nu(dx'),
                \qquad
                K_k^{m'}\mu(dx')=b(x')\,\nu(dx').
            \end{equation*}
            Now for any $A\in \mathcal{B}(\mathbb{X})$ with $K_k^{m'}\mu(A)>0$,
            \begin{equation*}
                \frac{K_k^{m}\mu(A)}{K_k^{m'}\mu(A)}
                =\frac{\int_A a(x')\,\nu(dx')}{\int_A b(x')\,\nu(dx')}
            \end{equation*}
            Writing $\underline{r}\coloneq\inf_{x'}\frac{a(x')}{b(x')}$ and
            $\overline{r}\coloneq\sup_{x'}\frac{a(x')}{b(x')}$, we see that for
            every $x'\in \mathbb{X}$
            \begin{gather*}
                \underline{r}\le \frac{a(x')}{b(x')}\le\overline{r}\\
                \iff \\
                \underline{r}\,b(x')\le a(x')\le\overline{r}\,b(x')
            \end{gather*}
            integrating over $A$ against $\nu$ gives
            \begin{gather}    
                \underline{r}\int\limits_{A}b(x')\nu(dx')
                \le
                \int\limits_{A} a(x')\nu (dx')
                \le
                \overline{r}\int\limits_{A} b(x')\nu (dx')\nonumber\\
                \iff \nonumber\\
                \underline{r}\le\frac{K_k^{m}\mu(A)}{K_k^{m'}\mu(A)}\le\overline{r}
                \label{eq:hilb_ineq}
            \end{gather}
            The same bounds hold with $A$ replaced by any Borel $B$. By definition
            of the Hilbert metric and \eqref{eq:hilb_ineq}
            \begin{equation*}
                h\bigl(K_k^{m}\mu,K_k^{m'}\mu\bigr)
                =\log\frac{\sup_{A}\frac{K_{k}^{m}\mu(A)}{K_{k}^{m'}\mu(A)}}
                {\inf_{A}\frac{K_{k}^{m}\mu(A)}{K_{k}^{m'}\mu(A)}}.
                =\log\left(\frac{\bar{r}}{\underline{r}}\right)
            \end{equation*}
            Assumption~\ref{ass:sensor_map_regularity}-(1) gives
            $|a(x')-b(x')|\le C_{\mathcal{O}}\,d_{\mathbb{M}}(m,m')$, and
            $a,b\ge\underline{o}$ by
            Assumption~\ref{ass:hilbert_mixing}-(2), so for every $x'$,
            \begin{equation*}
                \frac{a(x')}{b(x')}
                \le1+\frac{|a(x')-b(x')|}{b(x')}
                \le1+\frac{C_{\mathcal{O}}}{\underline{o}}\,
                d_{\mathbb{M}}(m,m').
            \end{equation*}
            Hence, using $\log(1+s)\le s$,
            \begin{align*}
                h\bigl(K_k^{m}\mu,K_k^{m'}\mu\bigr)
                &=\log\left(\frac{\overline{r}}{\underline{r}}\right)\\
                &\le \log \left( \frac{1+
                \frac{\mathcal{C}_{\mathcal{O}}}{\underline{o}}d_{\mathbb{M}}(m,m')}
                {\left(1+ \frac{\mathcal{C}_{\mathcal{O}}}
                {\underline{o}}d_{\mathbb{M}}(m,m')\right)^{-1}} \right)\\
                &\le2\log\!\Bigl(1+\tfrac{C_{\mathcal{O}}}{\underline{o}}\,
                d_{\mathbb{M}}(m,m')\Bigr)\\
                &\le\frac{2\,C_{\mathcal{O}}}{\underline{o}}\,
                d_{\mathbb{M}}(m,m')
                \eqqcolon\varepsilon,
            \end{align*}
            uniformly in $k$, the realization, and $\mu$.

            By construction the unnormalized measures
            advance one step at a time, $\pi_{k+1}^{m}=K_k^{m}\pi_k^{m}$ and
            $\pi_{k+1}^{m'}=K_k^{m'}\pi_k^{m'}$, so
            \begin{equation*}
                d_{k+1}
                =h\bigl(\pi_{k+1}^{m},\pi_{k+1}^{m'}\bigr)
                =h\bigl(K_k^{m}\pi_k^{m},\,K_k^{m'}\pi_k^{m'}\bigr).
            \end{equation*}
            Insert the intermediate measure $K_k^{m}\pi_k^{m'}$, which applies
            the map-$m$ operator to the map-$m'$ measure, and apply the triangle
            inequality for $h$:
            \begin{equation*}
                d_{k+1}
                \le\underbrace{h\bigl(K_k^{m}\pi_k^{m},\,
                K_k^{m}\pi_k^{m'}\bigr)}_{\text{(i)}}
                +\underbrace{h\bigl(K_k^{m}\pi_k^{m'},\,
                K_k^{m'}\pi_k^{m'}\bigr)}_{\text{(ii)}}.
            \end{equation*}
            Term (i) is a single operator $K_k^{m}$ applied to two different
            measures, so Lemma~\ref{lem:one_step_hilbert}-(2) gives the
            contraction
            \begin{equation*}
                \text{(i)}=h\bigl(K_k^{m}\pi_k^{m},\,K_k^{m}\pi_k^{m'}\bigr)
                \le\alpha\,h\bigl(\pi_k^{m},\pi_k^{m'}\bigr)
                =\alpha\,d_k.
            \end{equation*}
            Term (ii) is the two different operators $K_k^{m},K_k^{m'}$ applied
            to the single measure $\pi_k^{m'}$, which is the per-step discrepancy
            established above with $\mu=\pi_k^{m'}$, so
            \begin{equation*}
                \text{(ii)}=h\bigl(K_k^{m}\pi_k^{m'},\,K_k^{m'}\pi_k^{m'}\bigr)
                \le\varepsilon.
            \end{equation*}
            Combining, $d_{k+1}\le\alpha\,d_k+\varepsilon$ for every
            $k\ge0$. Iterating this recursion from $d_0=0$,
            \begin{equation*}
                d_N
                \le\varepsilon\sum_{j=0}^{N-1}\alpha^{j}
                \le\varepsilon\sum_{j=0}^{\infty}\alpha^{j}
                =\frac{\varepsilon}{1-\alpha}
                =\frac{2\,C_{\mathcal{O}}}{\underline{o}\,(1-\alpha)}\,
                d_{\mathbb{M}}(m,m'),
            \end{equation*}
            where the series converges since $\alpha<1$
            (Lemma~\ref{lem:one_step_hilbert}-(2)). This bound is uniform in the
            realized window and in $t$, as $\varepsilon$ and $\alpha$ depend on
            neither.
     
            The quantity $d_N$ is the Hilbert
            distance between the unnormalized measures $\pi_N^{m},\pi_N^{m'}$;
            by scale invariance of $h$ it equals the Hilbert distance between
            their normalizations, the two conditional pose laws
            \begin{equation*}
                \overline{\pi}_N^{m}
                =\mathbb{P}^{b^*}\bigl(X_{t+N}\in\cdot\mid M_{t+N}=m,\,h_t^N\bigr),
                \qquad
                \overline{\pi}_N^{m'}
                =\mathbb{P}^{b^*}\bigl(X_{t+N}\in\cdot\mid M_{t+N}=m',\,h_t^N\bigr).
            \end{equation*}
            Lemma~\ref{lem:hilbert_tv} bounds the total variation distance
            between these probability measures by the Hilbert distance,
            \begin{equation*}
                \bigl\lVert\overline{\pi}_N^{m}-\overline{\pi}_N^{m'}
                \bigr\rVert_{TV}
                \le\frac{2}{\log 3}\,d_N,
            \end{equation*}
            and on the compact space $\mathbb{X}$ the Wasserstein distance is
            controlled by the total variation distance,
            $W_1(\rho,\rho')\le\tfrac12\mathrm{diam}(\mathbb{X})
            \lVert\rho-\rho'\rVert_{TV}$. Hence,
            \begin{align*}
                W_1\bigl(\overline{\pi}_N^{m},\overline{\pi}_N^{m'}\bigr)
                &\le\frac{\mathrm{diam}(\mathbb{X})}{2}\,
                \bigl\lVert\overline{\pi}_N^{m}-\overline{\pi}_N^{m'}
                \bigr\rVert_{TV}
                \le\frac{\mathrm{diam}(\mathbb{X})}{2}\cdot
                \frac{2}{\log 3}\,d_N
                =\frac{\mathrm{diam}(\mathbb{X})}{\log 3}\,d_N\\
                &\le\frac{\mathrm{diam}(\mathbb{X})}{\log 3}\cdot
                \frac{2\,C_{\mathcal{O}}}{\underline{o}\,(1-\alpha)}\,
                d_{\mathbb{M}}(m,m').
            \end{align*}
            This is the claimed bound with
            \begin{equation*}
                L_{\mathbb{X}}
                =\frac{2\,\mathrm{diam}(\mathbb{X})\,C_{\mathcal{O}}}
                {\underline{o}\,(1-\alpha)\log 3}.
            \end{equation*}
            Since $\mathrm{diam}(\mathbb{X})$, $C_{\mathcal{O}}$,
            $\underline{o}$, and $\alpha$ are all independent of $N$, the
            realization, and $t$, so is $L_{\mathbb{X}}$.
        \end{proof}  
        \begin{remark}
            Note that the constant $L_{\mathbb{X}}$ is independent of $N$, the
            realized window, and $t$.
        \end{remark}
        With both (M.i) and (M.ii) shown to be bounded in terms of the 
        metric, the regularity of $g$ follows.
        \begin{lemma}
            \label{lem:g_lipschitz}
            Let Assumptions~\ref{ass:hilbert_mixing}
            and~\ref{ass:sensor_map_regularity} hold, and let
            $L_{\mathbb{X}}$ be the constant of
            Proposition~\ref{prop:pose_conditional_lipschitz}. Fix
            $N\ge1$, a realization $h_t^N$, and
            $f\in\mathrm{Lip}(\mathbb{S},1)$ with respect to
            $d_{\mathbb{S}}(s,s')=d_{\mathbb{X}}(x,x')
            +d_{\mathbb{M}}(m,m')$, and define, as in
            \eqref{eq:g_lipschitz_decomp},
            \begin{equation*}
                g(m)\coloneq\int_{\mathbb{X}}f(x,m)\,
                \mathbb{P}^{b^*}\bigl(X_{t+N}\in dx\mid
                M_{t+N}=m,\,h_t^N\bigr).
            \end{equation*}
            Then for all $m,m'\in\mathbb{M}$,
            \begin{equation*}
                |g(m)-g(m')|\le(1+L_{\mathbb{X}})\,d_{\mathbb{M}}(m,m').
            \end{equation*}
        \end{lemma}
        \begin{proof}
            Adding and subtracting
            $\int_{\mathbb{X}}f(x,m')\,
            \mathbb{P}^{b^*}(X_{t+N}\in dx\mid M_{t+N}=m,\,h_t^N)$ as in
            \eqref{eq:g_lipschitz_decomp} produces the two terms (M.i) and
            (M.ii). 

            For (M.i), since $f$ is $1$-Lipschitz with respect to
            $d_{\mathbb{S}}$, for each fixed $x$ we have
            $|f(x,m)-f(x,m')|\le d_{\mathbb{S}}((x,m),(x,m'))
            =d_{\mathbb{M}}(m,m')$, and since
            $\mathbb{P}^{b^*}(X_{t+N}\in\cdot\mid M_{t+N}=m,\,h_t^N)$ is a
            probability measure, integrating this pointwise bound gives
            $\text{(M.i)}\le d_{\mathbb{M}}(m,m')$, which is
            \eqref{eq:Mi_bound}. 

            For (M.ii), the map
            $x\mapsto f(x,m')$ is $1$-Lipschitz on
            $(\mathbb{X},d_{\mathbb{X}})$ for fixed $m'$, again by the
            product form of $d_{\mathbb{S}}$. Hence, by the
            Kantorovich--Rubinstein representation of $W_1$ on
            $\mathbb{X}$,
            \begin{align*}
                \text{(M.ii)}
                &=\biggl|\int_{\mathbb{X}}f(x,m')\,
                \bigl[\mathbb{P}^{b^*}(X_{t+N}\in dx\mid
                M_{t+N}=m,\,h_t^N)
                -\mathbb{P}^{b^*}(X_{t+N}\in dx\mid
                M_{t+N}=m',\,h_t^N)\bigr]\biggr|\\
                &\le W_1\Bigl(\mathbb{P}^{b^*}\bigl(X_{t+N}\in\cdot\mid
                M_{t+N}=m,\,h_t^N\bigr),\;
                \mathbb{P}^{b^*}\bigl(X_{t+N}\in\cdot\mid
                M_{t+N}=m',\,h_t^N\bigr)\Bigr)\\
                &\le L_{\mathbb{X}}\,d_{\mathbb{M}}(m,m'),
            \end{align*}
            the last step by
            Proposition~\ref{prop:pose_conditional_lipschitz}. Summing the
            two bounds concludes the proof.
        \end{proof}

        \subsubsection{Localization} \label{sub:localization} % (fold)
        The next lemma bounds the map term (M) by the Wasserstein distances of
        the two map posteriors to a common limit, with the common limit being
        the Dirac measure at some map element $\bar{m}\in \mathbb{M}$. This
        construction is in an effort toward eventually invoking posterior
        consistency which would drive both Wasserstein distance terms to zero,
        yielding the desired asymptotic filter stability property.

        \begin{lemma}
            \label{lem:localization}
            Let Assumptions~\ref{ass:hilbert_mixing}
            and~\ref{ass:sensor_map_regularity} hold. Then for every
            $N\ge1$, every realization $h_t^N$, and every
            $\bar{m}\in\mathbb{M}$,
            \begin{equation*}
                W_1\Bigl(\mathbb{P}^{b^*}\bigl(S_{t+N}\in\cdot\mid
                h_t^N\bigr),\,\lambda\Bigr)
                % &
                \le
                % (1+L_{\mathbb{X}})\biggl[
                % \int_{\mathbb{M}}d_{\mathbb{M}}(m,\bar{m})\,
                % \mathbb{P}^{b^*}\bigl(M_{t+N}\in dm\mid h_t^N\bigr)\\
                % &\qquad\qquad\qquad
                % +\int_{\mathbb{M}}d_{\mathbb{M}}(m,\bar{m})\,
                % \mathbb{P}^{b_t^-}\bigl(M_{t+N}\in dm\mid h_t^N\bigr)
                % \biggr]\\
                % &=
                (1+L_{\mathbb{X}})\left[
                W_{1}\bigl(\mathbb{P}^{b^{*}}(M_{t+N}\in\cdot\mid
                h_{t}^{N}),\delta_{\bar{m}}\bigr)
                \!+\!W_{1}\bigl(\mathbb{P}^{b^{-}_{t}}(M_{t+N}\in\cdot\mid
                h_{t}^{N}),\delta_{\bar{m}}\bigr)\right]
            \end{equation*}
            where $\lambda$ is the intermediate measure of
            Section~\ref{sub:W1_decomposition}.
        \end{lemma}
        \begin{proof}
            Fix $f\in\mathrm{Lip}(\mathbb{S},1)$ and let $g$ be as in
            Lemma~\ref{lem:g_lipschitz} yielding the disintegration expressed in
            equation~\eqref{eq:M_disintegration}. The two map posteriors are
            probability measures, so the constant function $m\mapsto
            g(\bar{m})$ integrates to $g(\bar{m})$ against each, and therefore
            to zero against their difference. Subtracting this zero,
            \begin{align*}
                &\int_{\mathbb{M}}g(m)\,
                \bigl[\mathbb{P}^{b^*}\bigl(M_{t+N}\in dm\mid h_t^N\bigr)
                -\mathbb{P}^{b_t^-}\bigl(M_{t+N}\in dm\mid
                h_t^N\bigr)\bigr]\\
                &=\int_{\mathbb{M}}\bigl[g(m)-g(\bar{m})\bigr]\,
                \mathbb{P}^{b^*}\bigl(M_{t+N}\in dm\mid h_t^N\bigr)
                -\int_{\mathbb{M}}\bigl[g(m)-g(\bar{m})\bigr]\,
                \mathbb{P}^{b_t^-}\bigl(M_{t+N}\in dm\mid h_t^N\bigr).
            \end{align*}
            By Lemma~\ref{lem:g_lipschitz},
            $|g(m)-g(\bar{m})|
            \le(1+L_{\mathbb{X}})\,d_{\mathbb{M}}(m,\bar{m})$ pointwise, so
            each integral is bounded in absolute value by
            $(1+L_{\mathbb{X}})\int d_{\mathbb{M}}(m,\bar{m})$ against the
            respective posterior. The resulting bound does not depend on
            $f$, taking the supremum over $f\in\mathrm{Lip}(\mathbb{S},1)$
            on the left concludes the proof.
        \end{proof}

        \subsubsection{Posterior consistency of the map marginals}
        \label{sub:map_consistency}

        Lemma~\ref{lem:localization} holds for an arbitrary
        $\bar{m}\in\mathbb{M}$, and we now set $\bar{m}=M$ as the true map:
        \begin{align}
            &W_1\Bigl(\mathbb{P}^{b^*}\bigl(S_{t+N}\in\cdot\mid h_t^N\bigr),
            \,\lambda\Bigr)\nonumber\\
            &\le(1+L_{\mathbb{X}})\Bigl[
            \underbrace{W_1\bigl(\mathbb{P}^{b^{*}}(M_{t+N}\in\cdot\mid
            h_t^N),\,\delta_{M}\bigr)}_{\text{reference posterior}}
            +\underbrace{W_1\bigl(\mathbb{P}^{b^{-}_{t}}(M_{t+N}\in\cdot\mid
            h_t^N),\,\delta_{M}\bigr)}_{\text{exact posterior}}
            \Bigr].
            \label{eq:map_term_at_truth}
        \end{align}
        The map term therefore vanishes once both map posteriors concentrate
        at $M$ as the window grows. 

        All randomness is on the probability space
        $(\Omega,\mathcal{F},\mathbb{P}^{\hat{\gamma}}_{b_0^-})$ carrying the
        true model under the policy $\hat{\gamma}$, with
        $S_0=(X_0,M)\sim b_0^-$. Write
        \begin{equation*}
            \mathcal{F}_s\coloneqq\sigma\bigl(Y_{[0,s]},\,U_{[0,s-1]}\bigr),
            \qquad
            \mathcal{F}_\infty\coloneqq\sigma\Bigl(\bigcup_{s\ge0}\mathcal{F}_s\Bigr),
        \end{equation*}
        Expectations
        $\mathbb{E}$ without superscript are under
        $\mathbb{P}^{\hat{\gamma}}_{b_0^-}$.

        \begin{assumption}[Measurable recovery of the true map]
            \label{ass:map_identifiability}
            There exists an $\mathcal{F}_\infty$-measurable
            $M':\Omega\to\mathbb{M}$ with $M=M'$
            $\mathbb{P}^{\hat{\gamma}}_{b_0^-}$-a.s.
        \end{assumption}

        \begin{remark}
            This assumption will later need to be proved. 
            \citet[Theorem~4.1]{miller2018doob} prove this by exploiting the
            iid nature of their setup. We will require an alternative approach
            due to our different setup.
        \end{remark}

        \begin{theorem}[Consistency of the exact posterior]
            \label{thm:exact_posterior_consistency}
            Let Assumption~\ref{ass:map_identifiability} hold. Then for
            $b_0^-|_{\mathbb{M}}$-almost every $m^{*}$,
            \begin{equation*}
                W_1\Bigl(\mathbb{P}^{b_t^-}\bigl(M_{t+N}\in\cdot\mid
                Y_{[t,t+N]},\,U_{[t,t+N-1]}\bigr),\,\delta_{m^{*}}\Bigr)
                \xrightarrow[N\to\infty]{}0
                \qquad
                \mathbb{P}^{\hat{\gamma}}_{b_0^-}
                \bigl(\,\cdot\mid M=m^{*}\bigr)\text{-a.s.}
            \end{equation*}
        \end{theorem}
        \begin{proof}

            \noindent\emph{Step 1 (reduction to a martingale).}

            \noindent By the composition property of the update
            map $\Psi$ established in 
            Section~\ref{sec:An Alternative Finite Window Approach}, with
            $b_t^-=\mathbb{P}^{\hat{\gamma}}_{b_0^-}(S_t\in\cdot\mid\mathcal{F}_t)$,
            \begin{align*}
                \mathbb{P}^{b_t^-}\bigl(S_{t+N}\in\cdot\mid
                Y_{[t,t+N]},U_{[t,t+N-1]}\bigr)
                &=\mathbb{P}^{b_0^-}\bigl(S_{t+N}\in\cdot\mid
                Y_{[0,t+N]},U_{[0,t+N-1]}\bigr)\\
                &=\mathbb{P}^{\hat{\gamma}}_{b_0^-}\bigl(S_{t+N}\in\cdot\mid
                \mathcal{F}_{t+N}\bigr)
            \end{align*}

            The map is static, so $M_{t+N}=M$ and the $\mathbb{M}$-marginal of
            equation above is the conditional distribution of $M$ itself. Let
            $\nu'_N:\Omega\times\mathcal{B}(\mathbb{M})\to[0,1]$ denote the
            $\mathbb{M}$-marginal of this updated belief. By the construction
            of the belief process in 
            Section~\ref{sec:An Alternative Finite Window Approach}, $\nu'_N$
            is a stochastic kernel, and it is a regular conditional
            distribution of $M$ given $\mathcal{F}_{t+N}$, namely
            \begin{equation}
                \nu'_N(\omega,\cdot)\in\mathcal{P}(\mathbb{M})
                \quad\forall\omega\in\Omega,
                \qquad
                \nu'_N(\cdot,A)
                =\mathbb{E}^{\hat{\gamma}}_{b_0^-}
                \bigl[\mathbbm{1}_{\{M\in A\}}\mid\mathcal{F}_{t+N}\bigr]
                \ \text{ a.s.}
                \quad\forall A\in\mathcal{B}(\mathbb{M}).
                \label{eq:rcd}
            \end{equation}

            The weak convergence claimed in Theorem~\ref{thm:exact_posterior_consistency}
            is, by definition, the statement
            \begin{equation}
                \int_{\mathbb{M}}\phi(m)\,\nu'_N(\omega,dm)
                \xrightarrow[N\to\infty]{}\phi\bigl(M(\omega)\bigr)
                \qquad\forall\phi\in C(\mathbb{M}).
                \label{eq:weak_target}
            \end{equation}
            Accordingly, for bounded Borel $\phi:\mathbb{M}\to\mathbb{R}$ define
            \begin{equation}
                Z^{\phi}_N\coloneqq
                \int_{\mathbb{M}}\phi(m)\,\nu'_N(\cdot,dm),
                \qquad\text{so that}\qquad
                Z^{\phi}_N
                =\mathbb{E}^{\hat{\gamma}}_{b_0^-}
                \bigl[\phi(M)\mid\mathcal{F}_{t+N}\bigr]
                \ \text{ a.s.}
                \label{eq:Zphi_identity}
            \end{equation}
            For $\phi=\mathbbm{1}_A$ the identity \eqref{eq:Zphi_identity} is
            \eqref{eq:rcd} itself, since
            \begin{equation*}
                Z^{\mathbbm{1}_A}_N
                =\int_{\mathbb{M}}\mathbbm{1}_A(m)\,\nu'_N(\cdot,dm)
                =\nu'_N(\cdot,A).
            \end{equation*}
            Linearity in $\phi$ extends it to simple functions,
            and monotone convergence, applied to $\nu'_N(\omega,\cdot)$ on the
            left and conditionally on the right, extends it to all bounded
            Borel $\phi$.

            Fix a bounded Borel $\phi$. We see that:
            \begin{enumerate}
                \item $|Z^{\phi}_N|\le\lVert\phi\rVert_\infty$ for all $N$,
                    and since we are on a probability space,
                    $Z^{\phi}_N\in L^1(\mathbb{P}^{\hat{\gamma}}_{b_0^-})$.
                \item $Z^{\phi}_N$ is $\mathcal{F}_{t+N}$-measurable, by
                    \eqref{eq:Zphi_identity} and the definition of conditional
                    expectation.
                \item By the iterated expectation, using
                    $\mathcal{F}_{t+N}\subseteq\mathcal{F}_{t+N+1}$,
                    \begin{align*}
                        \mathbb{E}^{\hat{\gamma}}_{b_0^-}
                        \bigl[Z^{\phi}_{N+1}\mid\mathcal{F}_{t+N}\bigr]
                        &=\mathbb{E}^{\hat{\gamma}}_{b_0^-}
                        \Bigl[\mathbb{E}^{\hat{\gamma}}_{b_0^-}
                        \bigl[\phi(M)\mid\mathcal{F}_{t+N+1}\bigr]
                        \,\Big|\,\mathcal{F}_{t+N}\Bigr]\\
                        &=\mathbb{E}^{\hat{\gamma}}_{b_0^-}
                        \bigl[\phi(M)\mid\mathcal{F}_{t+N}\bigr]
                        =Z^{\phi}_N
                        \qquad\text{a.s.}
                    \end{align*}
            \end{enumerate}
            Hence $(Z^{\phi}_N)_{N\ge1}$ is a bounded
            $(\mathcal{F}_{t+N})_{N\ge1}$-martingale.

            \emph{Step 2 (limit of $Z^{\phi}_N$).}
            By L\'evy's upward theorem,
            \begin{equation}
                Z^{\phi}_N\xrightarrow[N\to\infty]{}
                \mathbb{E}^{\hat{\gamma}}_{b_0^-}
                \bigl[\phi(M)\mid\mathcal{F}_\infty\bigr]
                \qquad\text{a.s.\ and in }L^1.
                \label{eq:levy_limit}
            \end{equation}
            Let $M'$ be as in Assumption~\ref{ass:map_identifiability}, so that
            $\phi(M)=\phi(M')$ a.s. Since $\phi(M')$ is
            bounded and $\mathcal{F}_\infty$-measurable
            \begin{equation*}
                \mathbb{E}^{\hat{\gamma}}_{b_0^-}
                \bigl[\phi(M)\mid\mathcal{F}_\infty\bigr]=
                \mathbb{E}^{\hat{\gamma}}_{b_0^-}
                \bigl[\phi(M')\mid\mathcal{F}_\infty\bigr]
                =\phi(M')=\phi(M)
                \qquad\text{a.s.}
            \end{equation*}
            the first equality since $\phi(M)=\phi(M')$ a.s., the second
            equality is due to the $\mathcal{F}_{\infty }$-measurability of
            $\phi(M')$, the third by Assumption~\ref{ass:map_identifiability}.
            With \eqref{eq:levy_limit} this gives $Z^{\phi}_N\to\phi(M)$ a.s.,
            that is,
            \begin{equation}
                \mathbb{P}^{\hat{\gamma}}_{b_0^-}\bigl(G_\phi\bigr)=1,
                \qquad
                G_\phi\coloneqq
                \bigl\{\omega\in\Omega:
                Z^{\phi}_N(\omega)\to\phi(M(\omega))\bigr\}.
                \label{eq:good_event}
            \end{equation}
            The probability in \eqref{eq:good_event} is well posed only if
            $G_\phi\in\mathcal{F}$. This holds since $Z^{\phi}_N$ and $\phi(M)$
            are random variables and 
            \begin{equation*}
                G_\phi=\bigcap_{j\ge1}\bigcup_{K\ge1}\bigcap_{N\ge K}
                \bigl\{\lvert Z^{\phi}_N-\phi(M)\rvert\le j^{-1}\bigr\},
            \end{equation*} a countable combination of events.

            \emph{Step 3 (one null set for all of $C(\mathbb{M})$).} 
            Weak convergence at a fixed $\omega$ means
            $Z^{\phi}_N(\omega)\to\phi(M(\omega))$ for every $\phi\in
            C(\mathbb{M})$, with one $\omega$ serving all $\phi$, so satisfying 
            \eqref{eq:weak_target} requires a single event of measure one
            contained in $G_\phi$ for every $\phi$. A natural choice is
            $\bigcap_{\phi\in C(\mathbb{M})}G_\phi$, but it is unusable as the
            family $\{G_\phi:\phi\in C(\mathbb{M})\}$ is uncountable, and a
            $\sigma$-algebra is closed under countable operations only, so the
            intersection need not be an event. Even when it is an event, an
            uncountable intersection of full-measure events can fail to carry
            full measure. For example, with $\lambda$ the Lebesgue measure on
            $[0,1]$,
            \begin{equation*}
                \lambda\bigl([0,1]\setminus\{x\}\bigr)=1
                \quad\forall x\in[0,1],
                \qquad\text{while}\qquad
                \bigcap_{x\in[0,1]}\bigl([0,1]\setminus\{x\}\bigr)=\emptyset.
            \end{equation*}
            We can circumvent this issue since 
            $(C(\mathbb{M}),\lVert\cdot\rVert_\infty)$ is separable which
            follows from the compactness of $\mathbb{M}$, this allows us to fix
            a countable dense $\{\phi_k\}_{k\ge1}\subseteq C(\mathbb{M})$ and
            set
            \begin{equation}
                G_0\coloneqq\bigcap_{k\ge1}G_{\phi_k},
                \qquad
                \mathbb{P}^{\hat{\gamma}}_{b_0^-}(G_0)
                \ge1-\sum_{k\ge1}
                \mathbb{P}^{\hat{\gamma}}_{b_0^-}
                \bigl(G_{\phi_k}^{c}\bigr)=1
                \label{eq:G0}
            \end{equation}
            where each $\mathbb{P}^{\hat{\gamma}}_{b_0^-}(G_{\phi_k}^{c})=0$ by
            \eqref{eq:good_event} applied at $\phi=\phi_k$.
            By density this applies to all of $C(\mathbb{M})$ for $\omega \in
            G_{0}$.

            Fix $\omega\in G_0$, $\phi\in C(\mathbb{M})$, and $\varepsilon>0$,
            and choose $k$ with
            $\lVert\phi-\phi_k\rVert_\infty<\varepsilon$. Since
            $\nu'_N(\omega,\cdot)\in\mathcal{P}(\mathbb{M})$,
            \begin{align*}
                \bigl|Z^{\phi}_N(\omega)-\phi\bigl(M(\omega)\bigr)\bigr|
                &= \bigl|Z^{\phi}_N(\omega) - Z^{\phi_{k}}_{N}(\omega) +
                Z^{\phi_{k}}_{N}(\omega)-\phi_{k}\bigl(M(\omega )\bigr) +
                    \phi_{k}\bigl(M(\omega )\bigr) -
                        \phi\bigl(M(\omega)\bigr)\bigr|\\
                &\le
                \underbrace{\bigl|Z^{\phi-\phi_k}_N(\omega)\bigr|}_{
                \le\lVert\phi-\phi_k\rVert_\infty<\varepsilon\ \forall N}
                +\bigl|Z^{\phi_k}_N(\omega)
                -\phi_k\bigl(M(\omega)\bigr)\bigr|
                +\underbrace{\bigl|\phi_k\bigl(M(\omega)\bigr)
                -\phi\bigl(M(\omega)\bigr)\bigr|}_{<\,\varepsilon},
            \end{align*}
            and the middle term vanishes as $N\to\infty$ since
            $\omega\in G_{\phi_k}$. Hence
            \begin{equation*}
                \limsup_{N\to\infty}
                \bigl|Z^{\phi}_N(\omega)-\phi\bigl(M(\omega)\bigr)\bigr|
                \le2\varepsilon
                \qquad\forall\varepsilon>0,
            \end{equation*}
            so \eqref{eq:weak_target} holds at every $\omega\in G_0$, i.e.
            \begin{equation}
                \nu'_N(\omega,\cdot)\to \delta_{M(\omega)}\text{ weakly}
                \qquad\forall\omega\in G_0.
                \label{eq:weak_on_G0}
            \end{equation}

            \emph{Step 4 (upgrade to $W_1$).}
            On the compact metric space $\mathbb{M}$ the metric $W_1$
            metrizes the weak convergence topology on
            $\mathcal{P}(\mathbb{M})$
            \citep[Theorem~6.9]{villani2008optimal}, so
            \eqref{eq:weak_on_G0} states
            \begin{equation*}
                W_1\bigl(\nu'_N(\omega,\cdot),\,\delta_{M(\omega)}\bigr)
                \xrightarrow[N\to\infty]{}0
                \qquad\forall\omega\in G_0.
            \end{equation*}
            
            \emph{Step 5 (disintegration over the prior).}
            Let
            $\mathbb{P}^{\hat{\gamma}}_{b_0^-}(\,\cdot\mid M=m^{*})$ be a
            stochastic kernel from $\mathbb{M}$ to $\Omega$ satisfying
            \begin{equation}
                \mathbb{P}^{\hat{\gamma}}_{b_0^-}
                \bigl(E\cap\{M\in A\}\bigr)
                =\int_{A}
                \mathbb{P}^{\hat{\gamma}}_{b_0^-}\bigl(E\mid M=m^{*}\bigr)\,
                b_0^-|_{\mathbb{M}}(dm^{*})
                \qquad
                \forall E\in\mathcal{F},\
                \forall A\in\mathcal{B}(\mathbb{M}),
                \label{eq:M_kernel}
            \end{equation}
            which exists since $(\Omega,\mathcal{F})$, is standard Borel, and
            regular conditional probabilities given any sub-$\sigma$-algebra
            exist on standard Borel spaces \citep[Theorem~8.5]{kallenberg2021},
            and where $b_0^-|_{\mathbb{M}}$ is the law of $M$ under
            $\mathbb{P}^{\hat{\gamma}}_{b_0^-}$ since $S_0=(X_0,M)\sim b_0^-$
            and the map is static.
            Disintegrating \eqref{eq:G0} via \eqref{eq:M_kernel} with $E=G_0$,
            $A=\mathbb{M}$,
            \begin{equation*}
                1=\mathbb{P}^{\hat{\gamma}}_{b_0^-}(G_0)
                =\int_{\mathbb{M}}
                \mathbb{P}^{\hat{\gamma}}_{b_0^-}\bigl(G_0\mid M=m^{*}\bigr)\,
                b_0^-|_{\mathbb{M}}(dm^{*}).
            \end{equation*}
            The function $g(m^{*})\coloneqq
            1-\mathbb{P}^{\hat{\gamma}}_{b_0^-}(G_0\mid M=m^{*})$ takes values in
            $[0,1]$ and, by the above expression,
            $\int_{\mathbb{M}}g\,db_0^-|_{\mathbb{M}}=1-1=0$. Markov's inequality then
            gives, for every $n\ge1$,
            \begin{equation*}
                b_0^-|_{\mathbb{M}}\bigl(g\ge n^{-1}\bigr)
                \le n\int_{\mathbb{M}}g\,db_0^-|_{\mathbb{M}}=0,
            \end{equation*}
            and since $\{g>0\}=\bigcup_{n\ge1}\{g\ge n^{-1}\}$,
            \begin{equation*}
                \mathbb{P}^{\hat{\gamma}}_{b_0^-}\bigl(G_0\mid M=m^{*}\bigr)=1
                \qquad b_0^-|_{\mathbb{M}}\text{-a.e. }m^{*}.
            \end{equation*}

            Moreover, testing \eqref{eq:M_kernel} on events
            $E=\{M\in A\}$ over a countable base of open sets $A$ and
            intersecting the resulting measure zero sets shows
            $\mathbb{P}^{\hat{\gamma}}_{b_0^-}(M=m^{*}\mid M=m^{*})=1$ for
            $b_0^-|_{\mathbb{M}}$-a.e. $m^{*}$. For every such $m^{*}$, the
            events $G_0$ and $\{M=m^{*}\}$ both carry full conditional measure,
            and at each $\omega$ in their intersection the conclusion of Step~4
            reads $W_1\bigl(\nu'_N(\omega,\cdot),\delta_{m^{*}}\bigr)\to0$,
            which is the assertion.

        \end{proof}

        % subsubsection Posterior consistency of the map marginals (end)

    % subsection Term (M): map marginal (end)

% section Filter Stability for Active SLAM (end)

Assume that we keep track of a finite window of observations parameterized
by $N\in \mathbb{Z}_{\ge0}$, i.e., we store a variable --- as defined
in \eqref{eq:history_var} --- which we denote now as $\hat{h}_{t}$.

Under the approximate scheme detailed in 
Section~\ref{sub:Approximation of the Information MDP} we can
equivalently refer to our information state
\eqref{eq:information_state} using this history variable
$\hat{h}_{t}$.

We would like to perform Q learning on this information MDP for which
we follow the usual Q learning algorithm such that for any $\hat{h}\in
\mathcal{D}^{N}$ and $u\in \mathbb{U}$,
\begin{equation}
    Q_{t+1}(\hat{h},u)=(1-\alpha_{t}(\hat{h},u))Q_{t}(\hat{h},u)+
    \alpha_{t}(\hat{h},u)\left( C_{t}(\hat{h},u)+\beta \min_{a\in
    \mathbb{U}}Q_{t}(h_{1}^{t},a) \right)
    \label{eq:Q_iterates}
\end{equation}

We now state the following assumption
\begin{assumption}
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item []
        \item $\mathbb{U},\mathbb{Y}$ are finite sets.
        \item Let $\alpha_{t}(\hat{h},u)=0$ unless
            $(\hat{h}_{t},u_{t})=(\hat{h},u)$. Furthermore,
            \begin{equation*}
                \alpha_{t}(\hat{h},u)= \frac{1}{1+\sum_{k=0}^{t}
                \mathbbm{1}_{\{ \hat{h}_{k}=\hat{h}, u_{k}=u \} }}
            \end{equation*}
            and with probability $1$, $\sum_{t} \alpha_{t}(\hat{h},u)=\infty$.
        \item Under the exploration
            policy $\gamma$ and initialization $S_{0}$. The controlled state
            and control action joint process $\{ S_{t}, U_{t} \}$ is
            asymptotically ergodic in the sense that for any measurable and
            bounded function $f$ we have that
            \begin{equation*}
                \lim_{N \to \infty} \frac{1}{N} \sum_{t=0}^{N-1} f(S_{t},U_{t})
                =\int\limits f(s,u) \pi^{\gamma}(ds,du) 
            \end{equation*}
            for some invariant measure on the hidden state and actions
            induced by the exploration policy $\pi^{\gamma}\in
            \mathcal{P}(\mathbb{S}\times \mathbb{U})$. 
        \item We have that $\forall s \in \mathbb{S},\forall O\in
            \mathcal{B}(\mathbb{Y})\setminus \emptyset :\mathcal{O}(O \mid
            s)>0$.
        \item The joint process
            $(\hat{h}_{t+1},\hat{h}_{t},U_{t},C_{t})_{t\ge0}$ is asymptotically
            ergodic in the sense that for the given initialization variable
            $\hat{h}_{0}$, for any measurable bounded function $f$, we have
            with probability one,
            \begin{equation*}
                \frac{1}{N}\sum_{t=0}^{N-1} f(\hat{h}_{t+1},\hat{h}_{t},U_{t},C_{t})
                \to \int\limits f(h',h,u,c)\,\pi(d \hat{h}',d \hat{h},du,dc) 
            \end{equation*}
            for some measure $\pi$ such that $\pi(\mathcal{D}^{N}\times
            \hat{h}\times u\times \mathbb{R})>0$ for all $(\hat{h},u)\in
            \mathcal{D}^{N}\times \mathbb{U}$.
    \end{enumerate}
    \label{ass:Q}
\end{assumption}
We note that a sufficient condition for the ergodicity assumption, for
every initialization of $S_{0}$, would be positive Harris recurrence under
the exploration policy.

\begin{theorem}[\cite{kara2024pomdp}]
    Under Assumption~\ref{ass:Q} the iterations in \eqref{eq:Q_iterates}
    converges almost surely.
\end{theorem}

## What the paper requires (implementation mapping)

From *Learning Near-Optimal Solutions to Active SLAM with Finite Memory*:

| Paper object | Implementation |
|---|---|
| Information state \(I_t=(b_{t-N}^-, h_t^N)\) | `InformationMDP` with predictor + window |
| \(\Psi(I)\mapsto b_t\) | Bayesian filter over window (reuse discrete filter ideas from BeliefMDP_n `F`, not Reznik codebook) |
| Cost \(\hat\rho(I,u)=\rho(\Psi(I),u)\) | belief exploration \(r\) + expected state cost \(c\) |
| Approx MDP \(\hat I_t=(b^*,h_t^N)\) | `ApproximateInformationMDP`; effective state = finite window \(h\in\mathcal{D}^N\) |
| Finite \(\mathbb{Y},\mathbb{U}\) (Ass. Q) | **quantize continuous Y/U** via existing quantizers; treat \(Y_n,U_n\) as the paper’s finite alphabets (aligned with KBY25 continuous-observation follow-up) |
| Q-learning (eq. Q iterates) | tabular updates on \((\hat h,u)\) with visit counts \(\alpha_t\) |

Paper-incomplete pieces (theory only for now): map identifiability assumption, empty contributions/sims. Code does not depend on finishing those proofs.

## Continuous spaces: explicit rule

1. Build continuous generative POMDP (existing models).
2. Fix lattices \(Y_n=\mathrm{quantize}(Y)\), \(U_n=\mathrm{quantize}(U)\) (reuse [`ObservationQuantizer`](src/classes/quantizer.py), [`ActionQuantizer`](src/classes/quantizer.py)).
3. All information-MDP / Q-learning APIs see only finite \(Y_n,U_n\); window size \(N\) yields \(|\mathcal{D}^N|=|Y_n|^{N+1}|U_n|^N\).
4. Optional later: also quantize pose/map support so \(\Psi\) runs on a finite simplex (same as BeliefMDP_n’s discrete filter)—needed for tractable \(\Psi\) and costs.

## Core API to build

Under `src/info_mdp/`:

1. **`window.py`** — sliding \(h_t^N=\{y_{[t-N,t]},u_{[t-N,t-1]}\}\) encode/decode to integer indices for tabular Q.
2. **`information_mdp.py`**
   - `InformationMDP`: stores evolving predictor \(b^-\), window; methods `psi`, `stage_cost`, `step` (true \(\overline\eta\)).

3. **`costs.py`** — thin wrappers around existing exploration costs (Shannon / \(\tilde W_1\)) + control effort, matching \(\rho=r+\int c\,b\). Prefer extracting shared cost helpers from [`belief_mdp_n.py`](src/classes/belief_mdp_n.py) only if needed; otherwise call duplicated small utilities inside `info_mdp` to avoid coupling.
4. **`q_learning.py`** — `FiniteMemoryQLearning` implementing Ass. Q + iterate (Q): exploration policy (ε-greedy / random), visit-based \(\alpha\), almost-sure tabular update; returns greedy policy on windows.
5. **`env.py`** — simulator: true state \((x,m)\), emit continuous \(y\), quantize to \(y_n\), advance window, return \((\hat h,u,C_t,\hat h')\).

Start with **active mapping, pose known** + **finite landmark map** ([`LandmarkMap`](src/classes/mapping.py) / existing toy configs). Reasons:

- Paper’s TV filter-stability path applies when \(\mathbb{M}\) is finite; continuous-map Wasserstein theory is unfinished.

Localization / full SLAM come after the mapping Q-learning loop works.

"""Simulators that interface information MDPs with a generative mapping POMDP."""

from __future__ import annotations

from typing import Any

import numpy as np

from .factory import MappingBackend
from .information_mdp import ApproximateInformationMDP, InformationMDP
from .window import FiniteHistoryWindow


def _smoothstep01(z: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
    z = np.clip(z, 0.0, 1.0)
    return 3.0 * z**2 - 2.0 * z**3


class MappingInfoEnv:
    """Known-pose active mapping environment for finite-memory Q-learning.

    Hidden map is static; pose is known to the filter. Continuous measurements
    and actions are quantized to (Y_n, U_n) before entering the information window.
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        backend: MappingBackend,
        approx_mdp: ApproximateInformationMDP,
        *,
        seed: int | None = None,
    ):
        self.backend = backend
        self.approx = approx_mdp
        self.spec = approx_mdp.spec
        self.rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)

        self.sensor = backend.mdp.sensor
        self.dt = float(backend.mdp.motion_model.dt)
        bounds = backend.mdp.state_bounds
        bounds = bounds.get() if hasattr(bounds, "get") else np.asarray(bounds)
        self.lower = np.asarray(bounds[:, 0], dtype=float)
        self.upper = np.asarray(bounds[:, 1], dtype=float)
        cov = backend.mdp.cov_x
        self.cov_x = cov.get() if hasattr(cov, "get") else np.asarray(cov, dtype=float)
        self.state_dim = int(self.cov_x.shape[0])

        self.window = FiniteHistoryWindow(self.spec)
        self.pose_hist = np.zeros((self.spec.n_obs_slots, self.state_dim), dtype=float)
        self.x = np.zeros(self.state_dim, dtype=float)
        self.true_map = None
        self.true_map_idx = None

        # Exact information MDP (optional diagnostics; shares alphabet/backend)
        self.exact = InformationMDP(
            backend,
            self.spec.N,
            lam=approx_mdp.lam,
            exploration_type=approx_mdp.exploration_type,
        )

    def _detection_probability(self, ranges: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
        eps = float(self.sensor.epsilon)
        r0 = float(self.sensor.r0)
        r1 = float(self.sensor.r1)
        r_max = float(self.sensor.r_max)
        eta_in = np.where(
            ranges <= eps,
            0.0,
            np.where(ranges >= r0, 1.0, _smoothstep01((ranges - eps) / (r0 - eps))),
        )
        eta_out = np.where(
            ranges <= r1,
            0.0,
            np.where(ranges >= r_max, 1.0, _smoothstep01((ranges - r1) / (r_max - r1))),
        )
        return np.clip(eta_in * (1.0 - eta_out), 0.0, 1.0)

    def _sample_truncated_range(self, mu: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
        eps = float(self.sensor.epsilon)
        r_max = float(self.sensor.r_max)
        sigma_r = float(self.sensor.sigma_r)
        samples = mu + self.rng.normal(0.0, sigma_r, size=mu.shape)
        invalid = (samples < eps) | (samples > r_max)
        while np.any(invalid):
            samples[invalid] = mu[invalid] + self.rng.normal(
                0.0, sigma_r, size=int(np.sum(invalid))
            )
            invalid = (samples < eps) | (samples > r_max)
        return samples

    def observe(self, x: np.ndarray, true_map: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
        """Sample a continuous range-bearing observation, flattened."""
        x = np.asarray(x, dtype=float).ravel()
        true_map = np.asarray(true_map, dtype=float)
        if true_map.ndim == 1:
            true_map = true_map.reshape(-1, 2)
        delta = true_map - x[:2]
        ranges = np.sqrt((delta**2).sum(axis=1))
        bearings = np.arctan2(delta[:, 1], delta[:, 0])
        L = true_map.shape[0]
        p_det = self._detection_probability(ranges)
        detected = self.rng.random(L) < p_det
        z = np.full((L, 2), np.nan)
        if np.any(detected):
            z[detected, 0] = self._sample_truncated_range(ranges[detected])
            phi = bearings[detected] + self.rng.normal(
                0.0, float(self.sensor.sigma_phi), size=int(np.sum(detected))
            )
            z[detected, 1] = np.arctan2(np.sin(phi), np.cos(phi))
        return z.ravel()

    def _step_pose(self, x: np.ndarray, u: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
        w = self.rng.multivariate_normal(np.zeros(self.state_dim), self.cov_x)
        return np.clip(x + u * self.dt + w, self.lower, self.upper)

    def reset(
        self,
        true_map: np.ndarray | int | None = None,
        x0: np.ndarray | None = None,
    ) -> tuple[int, dict[str, Any]]:
        if true_map is None:
            self.true_map_idx = int(self.rng.integers(0, self.backend.len_M))
            self.true_map = self.backend.all_maps[self.true_map_idx]
        elif isinstance(true_map, (int, np.integer)):
            self.true_map_idx = int(true_map)
            self.true_map = self.backend.all_maps[self.true_map_idx]
        else:
            self.true_map = np.asarray(true_map, dtype=float)
            self.true_map_idx = None

        if x0 is None:
            self.x = np.zeros(self.state_dim, dtype=float)
            self.x[:2] = 5.0
        else:
            self.x = np.asarray(x0, dtype=float).ravel().copy()

        y_cont = self.observe(self.x, self.true_map)
        y_idx = self.backend.observation_index(y_cont)
        self.window.reset(y_idx)
        self.pose_hist[:] = self.x
        h_idx = self.window.encode()
        self.exact.reset(None, y_idx, self.x)
        info = {
            "y_idx": y_idx,
            "x": self.x.copy(),
            "belief": self.approx.psi(self.window.y_hist, self.pose_hist),
        }
        return h_idx, info

    def step(self, u_idx: int) -> tuple[int, float, int, dict[str, Any]]:
        """Take action u_idx; return (h, cost, h', info)."""
        u_idx = int(u_idx)
        h_idx = self.window.encode()
        u = self.backend.U_n[u_idx]

        cost = self.approx.stage_cost(h_idx, u_idx, self.pose_hist)

        x_next = self._step_pose(self.x, u)
        y_cont = self.observe(x_next, self.true_map)
        y_idx = self.backend.observation_index(y_cont)

        self.window.push(y_idx, u_idx)
        if self.spec.N == 0:
            self.pose_hist[0] = x_next
        else:
            self.pose_hist[:-1] = self.pose_hist[1:]
            self.pose_hist[-1] = x_next
        self.x = x_next
        self.exact.push(y_idx, u_idx, x_next)

        h_next = self.window.encode()
        belief = self.approx.psi(self.window.y_hist, self.pose_hist)
        info = {

        return h_idx, float(cost), h_next, info

"""Finite-memory Q-learning for the approximate information MDP.

Implements the paper's Ass. Q visit-count stepsize and tabular update
    Q <- (1-a) Q + a (C + beta min_a' Q(h', a'))
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from typing import Literal

import numpy as np

from .env import MappingInfoEnv
from .information_mdp import ApproximateInformationMDP


class FiniteMemoryQLearning:
    """Tabular Q-learning on finite windows (hat h, u)."""

    def __init__(
        self,
        approx_mdp: ApproximateInformationMDP,
        env: MappingInfoEnv,
        *,
        beta: float = 0.95,
        epsilon: float = 0.2,
        exploration: Literal["epsilon_greedy", "random"] = "epsilon_greedy",
        seed: int | None = None,
    ):
        if not (0.0 < beta < 1.0):
            raise ValueError("beta must lie in (0, 1)")
        self.approx = approx_mdp
        self.env = env
        self.beta = float(beta)
        self.epsilon = float(epsilon)
        self.exploration = exploration
        self.rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)

        self.n_states = approx_mdp.n_states
        self.n_actions = approx_mdp.n_actions
        self.Q = np.zeros((self.n_states, self.n_actions), dtype=float)
        self.visits = np.zeros((self.n_states, self.n_actions), dtype=np.int64)
        self.episode_returns: list[float] = []
        self.td_errors: list[float] = []

    def alpha(self, h_idx: int, u_idx: int) -> float:
        """Visit-count stepsize 1 / (1 + #visits)."""
        return 1.0 / (1.0 + float(self.visits[h_idx, u_idx]))

    def select_action(self, h_idx: int) -> int:
        if self.exploration == "random" or self.rng.random() < self.epsilon:
            return int(self.rng.integers(0, self.n_actions))
        return int(np.argmin(self.Q[h_idx]))

    def greedy_action(self, h_idx: int) -> int:
        return int(np.argmin(self.Q[h_idx]))

    def update(self, h_idx: int, u_idx: int, cost: float, h_next: int) -> float:
        """One Q-learning update; returns absolute TD error."""
        a = self.alpha(h_idx, u_idx)
        target = float(cost) + self.beta * float(np.min(self.Q[h_next]))
        td = target - float(self.Q[h_idx, u_idx])
        self.Q[h_idx, u_idx] = (1.0 - a) * self.Q[h_idx, u_idx] + a * target
        self.visits[h_idx, u_idx] += 1
        self.td_errors.append(abs(td))
        return abs(td)

    def train_episode(
        self,
        horizon: int,
        *,
        true_map: np.ndarray | int | None = None,
        x0: np.ndarray | None = None,
    ) -> dict:
        h, _ = self.env.reset(true_map=true_map, x0=x0)
        total_cost = 0.0
        for _ in range(int(horizon)):
            u = self.select_action(h)
            h_cur, cost, h_next, _ = self.env.step(u)
            self.update(h_cur, u, cost, h_next)
            total_cost += float(cost)
            h = h_next
        self.episode_returns.append(total_cost)
        return {"return": total_cost, "final_h": h}

    def train(
        self,
        n_episodes: int,
        horizon: int,
        *,
        true_maps: list | None = None,
        verbose: bool = False,
    ) -> np.ndarray:
        """Run multiple episodes; optionally cycle through provided true maps."""
        for ep in range(int(n_episodes)):
            true_map = None
            if true_maps is not None and len(true_maps) > 0:
                true_map = true_maps[ep % len(true_maps)]
            info = self.train_episode(horizon, true_map=true_map)
            if verbose and (ep % max(1, n_episodes // 10) == 0 or ep == n_episodes - 1):
                print(f"episode {ep}: return={info['return']:.4f}")
        return self.Q

    def greedy_policy(self) -> np.ndarray:
        """Return argmin_u Q(h, u) for each window index."""
        return np.argmin(self.Q, axis=1).astype(np.int64)

    def rollout_greedy(
        self,
        horizon: int,
        *,
        true_map: np.ndarray | int | None = None,
        x0: np.ndarray | None = None,
        epsilon: float = 0.0,
    ) -> dict:
        """Evaluate the current greedy (or epsilon-greedy) policy without learning."""
        old_eps = self.epsilon
        old_expl = self.exploration
        self.epsilon = float(epsilon)
        self.exploration = "epsilon_greedy"
        h, info0 = self.env.reset(true_map=true_map, x0=x0)
        costs = []
        entropies = [float(-np.sum(info0["belief"] * np.log(np.maximum(info0["belief"], 1e-300))))]
        for _ in range(int(horizon)):
            u = self.select_action(h) if epsilon > 0 else self.greedy_action(h)
            _, cost, h, info = self.env.step(u)
            costs.append(float(cost))
            b = info["belief"]
            entropies.append(float(-np.sum(b * np.log(np.maximum(b, 1e-300)))))
        self.epsilon = old_eps
        self.exploration = old_expl
        return {
            "costs": np.asarray(costs),
            "entropies": np.asarray(entropies),
            "total_cost": float(np.sum(costs)),
        }

def test_window_spec_cardinality_N0():

    assert spec.n_action_slots == 0


def test_window_spec_cardinality_N1():
    spec = WindowSpec(n_y=4, n_u=3, N=1)
    # |Y|^2 * |U|^1
    assert spec.cardinality == 4 * 4 * 3


def test_encode_decode_roundtrip_N0():
    spec = WindowSpec(n_y=7, n_u=2, N=0)
    for y in range(spec.n_y):
        idx = encode_window([y], [], spec)
        y_hist, u_hist = decode_window(idx, spec)
        assert y_hist.tolist() == [y]
        assert u_hist.tolist() == []


def test_encode_decode_roundtrip_N2():
    spec = WindowSpec(n_y=3, n_u=2, N=2)
    rng = np.random.default_rng(0)
    for _ in range(50):
        y_hist = rng.integers(0, spec.n_y, size=spec.n_obs_slots)
        u_hist = rng.integers(0, spec.n_u, size=spec.n_action_slots)
        idx = encode_window(y_hist, u_hist, spec)
        y2, u2 = decode_window(idx, spec)
        np.testing.assert_array_equal(y2, y_hist)
        np.testing.assert_array_equal(u2, u_hist)


def test_finite_history_window_push_and_encode():

import numpy as np

def test_shannon_entropy_uniform():

def test_shannon_entropy_dirac():
